narrative_prose: The generator room was dim, lit only by the diagnostic screens' sickly green flicker. Ryn watched the erratic readouts of the magnetohydrodynamic Kelvin-Helmholtz shear across the ferrofluid sea, her jaw set tight. The low rumble of the turbines vibrated through the metal grating beneath her boots, a constant physical reminder of the colony's fragile equilibrium. She reached toward the primary control terminal, an array of heavy switches that governed the distribution flow. Above, a massive reinforced vent designed to channel excess thermal venting offered a grimly defensive position. Nearby, a precarious stack of auxiliary cooling coils threatened to consume any loose debris caught in their intake. She paused, recalibrating the flow rates manually, her fingers dancing over the worn dials. Silas stepped from the shadows, the soft hiss of the pneumatic door the only warning. Ryn exhaled, physically pressing the rusted access key into his palm. 'Your shift,' she murmured, the metal cool against her skin.
